items.title: From an invariant Markov kernel to its genuine L2 observable operator

source.attribution: ASTIS standard source-neutral mathematical derivation built on pinned Mathlib (Apache2.0). PBPS by Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang motivates the two actual adapters; no numbered paper theorem is attributed to this generic premise bundle.

source.anchor: Finite invariant Markov kernels, compProd, real L2 quotient and adjoint; motivating A.2/A.9 and B.1

items.statement: Let \(X\) be an arbitrary measurable space, \(\mu\) a finite measure (possibly zero), and \(\kappa\) a measurable Markov kernel with \(\mu\kappa=\mu\). There exists ONE continuous real-linear operator \(P:L^2(\mu)\to L^2(\mu)\), of norm at most one, such that for EVERY real \(f\) with \(f\in L^2(\mu)\), its kernel fibers are integrable for \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\) and \((P[f])(x)=\int f(z)\,\kappa(x,dz)\) almost everywhere. The operator preserves almost-everywhere order positivity, the constant-one class and the genuine integral of every L2 observable. IF \(\kappa\) is reversible for \(\mu\), this SAME operator is self-adjoint. No topology, separability, Standard-Borel or nonempty hypothesis is imposed. Exceptional sets may depend on f.
assumptions: Finite measure is a mathematical premise of this shared interface, not a hidden paper hypothesis. Finite mass need not equal one; it makes every L2 representative L1, so the mean equality is genuine. The zero target and empty carrier are allowed.

A kernel is genuinely measurable and every fiber is a probability measure. Its invariance is a premise here; an actual PBPS adapter must PRODUCE that premise from the verified actual process/kernel, never add invariance as a new paper-level assumption.

Lp is a quotient by mu-almost-everywhere equality. The theorem quantifies over every MemLp representative and concludes both AE fiber integrability and the AE kernel-integral formula. It asserts neither everywhere integrability nor an exceptional set uniform in all observables.
Order positivity means f>=0 AE implies Pf>=0 AE. It does not assert the Hilbert positive-semidefinite inequality <f,Pf>>=0. Mere invariance does not imply detailed balance or self-adjointness.
This is a standard source-neutral library theorem motivated by PBPS A.2/A.9 and B.1, not a claim that either paper section or the actual L2 adapter has been completed.

formulae.label: One operator, all representatives; optional self-adjointness
formulae.tex: \begin{gathered}(Pf)(x)=\int f(z)\,\kappa(x,dz)\quad(\mu\text{-a.e.}),\qquad\|P\|_{2\to2}\le1,\\ P1=1,\quad f\ge0\Rightarrow Pf\ge0\ (\mu\text{-a.e.}),\quad\int Pf\,d\mu=\int f\,d\mu,\\ \kappa\text{ reversible}\ \Longrightarrow\ P^*=P.\end{gathered}
